title: A Helping Hand & Hard/Soft 'c'

scenes.t: {name} reads about Sara. One sunny day, Sara went to the park because she was bored.
She drew a picture with her pencil. She was happy and smiled at her friend.
Then she fell and hurt her knee. Sara felt sad and scared.
Her friend helped her stand up.
Sara said, 'Thank you', and smiled again. Now she was tired, but she felt better.
We use 'then' to tell what happens next, 'but' to show something different, and 'and' to add more.
'c' is hard /k/ before a, o, u: cat, cold, cup. 'c' is soft /s/ before e, i, y: city, ice, face, pencil.

activities.title: Memory Game
activities.prompt: Match the verb with its past form.

why.k: c before a, o, u says /k/.
why.s: c before e, i, y says /s/.

items.q: She (fall / fell) and hurt her knee.
How did Sara feel when she fell?
She was hurt, ___ her friend helped her.
Sara played on the swings. ___ she fell.
Which word has a SOFT c?
Which word has a HARD c?

o: She drew a picture with her pencil?
She drew a picture with her pencil.
she drew a picture with her pencil

source: English – Primary 3 – Term 1 (Ministry of Education) pp. 74–77
